families.name: Johnson 1892
families.description: An ornamental display face with rounded strokes, knob-ended curls, and an irregular rhythm.
families.observed: A–Z, a–z and 0–9 from the 1892 patent and period foundry specimens. Larger impressions inform title-critical forms.
families.reconstructed: Punctuation and symbols are newly drawn companions. Spacing is adapted for digital use.

sources.title: Herman Ihlenburg, US design patent D21,607 (1892), alphabet and figures
sources.rights: Historical US patent plate; the patent states a seven-year term beginning 7 June 1892

sources.title: MacKellar, Smiths & Jordan, Specimens of Printing Types (1892), p. 274
sources.rights: Internet Archive records this 1892 edition as NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT

sources.title: H. Berthold specimen catalogue (1909), Zierschrift Skandia, p. 428
sources.rights: 1909 historical printing, treated as public domain in the supplied source record; publication predates the maximum US term

revival.notes: Historical scans were deskewed, debris removed, and outlines fitted to the impressions. Original baseline irregularities and curled terminals are retained.

families.name: Nero 1888
families.description: A condensed, chiseled display face with pointed terminals, deep notches, and dramatic descenders.
families.observed: Capitals A C D E F G H I K L M N O P R S T U V W; lowercase a c d e f g h i l m n o p r s t u v x y; numerals 0–9.
families.reconstructed: B J Q X Y Z and b j k q w z; modern punctuation, symbols, accented extensions and ligatures. Reconstructed forms follow the observed stroke vocabulary.

sources.title: The Inland Printer, vol. 6, no. 2 (November 1888), p. 141
sources.rights: US publication from 1888, beyond the maximum copyright term; scan supplied with the revival as public domain

sources.title: John Ryan Foundry, Latest and Standard Faces in Type (1894), p. 135
sources.rights: US publication from 1894, beyond the maximum copyright term; scan supplied with the revival as public domain

revival.notes: Historical impressions are cleaned and harmonised into one display master. Reconstructed characters are informed by the observed letters.
